India nears Chile trade deal, advances talk with Canada
content:
India is nearing an FTA with Chile, while talks with Canada are progressing and SACU negotiations have begun, Piyush Goyal said. 
India also seeks expanded trade ties with Mercosur and other partners. 
Talks with GCC and Israel remain slow amid regional tensions, while US negotiations continue. 
India has developed manuals to strengthen institutional capacity for handling trade negotiations.

title: China's major industrial profits rise 15.5% in Jan-Sept 2026
content:
China’s major industrial firms’ profits rose 15.5 per cent year on year in the first nine months of 2026, while September profits increased 14.4 per cent. 
High-tech manufacturing profits surged 52 per cent, accounting for 25.5 per cent of total industrial profits, as policy support and advanced manufacturing drove growth. 
Sustained growth hinges on domestic demand and broader industrial recovery.

title: India & Mexico to launch PTA talks to counter tariffs of up to 50%
content:
India and Mexico will launch PTA negotiations this week to secure preferential market access for Indian exporters facing Mexican tariffs of up to 50 per cent on 1,463 product categories. 
Bilateral trade reached $7.83 billion in FY26. 
The proposed pact will focus on selected goods, while India advances trade talks with other partners, including Chile, Canada, the US and Mercosur.

title: South Indian cotton yarn sees mixed trend as cotton prices weaken
content:
South India cotton yarn prices were mixed: Tiruppur combed yarn eased ₹3–5 (~$0.03–0.05) per kg as domestic and ICE cotton prices fell, while select Mumbai varieties rose ₹2–4 per kg on limited supply.
Gujarat cotton dropped ₹500–1,000 per candy as mills delayed purchases amid weak ICE futures and payment constraints.
All-India arrivals were 68,000–72,000 bales; Gujarat recorded 18,000–19,000.

title: Bangladesh's trade deficit widens 34% to $27.29 bn, a 3-year high
content:
Bangladesh’s trade deficit widened 34 per cent to $27.29 billion in FY26 as imports rose 10.5 per cent and exports declined slightly. 
China and India accounted for the largest bilateral gaps. 
With garments making up 80.62 per cent of exports, the government is developing strategies for 18 key markets to diversify products, boost competitiveness and expand regional trade links.

title: ICE cotton tumbles as rising stocks and firm dollar pressure prices
content:
ICE cotton fell sharply as faster US harvesting, a firm dollar and rising stocks pushed December 2026 below range; it settled at 79.06 cents, down 1.42 per cent.
US harvest reached 52 per cent by October 25, above five-year average; stocks rose to 27,865 bales and volume was the highest since October 9.
Markets await the Federal Reserve, fund rolls and possible Indian duty-free import extension.

title: Cambodia overtakes India in 9 US apparel categories: $770 mn swing
content:
Cambodia overtook India in nine US garment categories in January-August 2026 after a $770 million reversal in import values, TexPro shows.
Its import value rose 8.06 per cent to about $2.02 billion, while India fell 24.05 per cent to about $1.95 billion.
China’s August rebound masked a 26.85 per cent January-August fall, while higher US apparel tariffs failed to produce clear sourcing winners.

title: Türkiye loses €117 mn in EU denim. Who gets Europe’s jeans orders?
content:
TexPro shows China almost level with Türkiye in Europe’s cotton-bottoms trade, with EU imports under HS 620342 and 620462 up 2.56 per cent to $9.88 billion in January–July 2026.
Türkiye fell 9.84 per cent to $1.158 billion; China rose 19.36 per cent to $1.150 billion, with a $7.76 million gap.
Egypt expanded 43.60 per cent and Vietnam advanced 36.98 per cent; women’s bottoms outpaced men’s.
